about: World Pulse data. One entry per running story (thread), each with a dated log of updates. Add to it, never rewrite history: new facts go in as a new update. Run build_pulse.py after editing.

threads.title: Starship Flight 15

updates.text: Launched from Starbase. Booster 22 turned back for a tower catch, found a guidance problem, diverted over the Gulf and broke apart just before the water. Ship 42 reached orbit.

Ship 42 is still in orbit about 275 km up. It released 26 Starlink satellites and passed health checks over Hawaii and Chile. Final check about 2:29 pm Eastern; tower catch planned about 4:20 pm Eastern.
One live blog (drohnen.de) says a ship engine failed and the flight was cut to 3 hours. Nobody else reports it.
Ship 42 came home and was caught by the tower's arms at Starbase. It is the first time SpaceX has caught a Starship upper stage back from orbit. The flight lasted about 22 and a half hours.
The drohnen.de claim of a ship engine failure and a 3 hour flight is contradicted. CNBC reports the ship circled the Earth 14 times before landing on the tower.

Recaps say Ship 42 was caught about 22 hours 33 minutes after liftoff, after 14 orbits. Booster 22 called off its own catch and came down in the Gulf of Mexico. No date for Flight 16 has been announced.

No Flight 16 date yet. NASASpaceFlight says December is the aim, possibly the first Starship launch from pad 39A in Florida, with Booster 23 and Ship 43. Some sites now say early 2027. Musk says losing Booster 22 does not change the plan.

Still no Flight 16 date. It is aimed at no earlier than December 2026, from pad 39A in Florida, and no launch licence had been announced as of 16 Nov. Musk says the next flight will try to catch both the ship and the booster. He also describes a bigger next version (V4), about 70 metres tall with over 60% more fuel.
Still no Flight 16 date from SpaceX. One launch tracker now says early 2027 is more likely than December; not confirmed.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.
Third scan with nothing new. Still no Flight 16 date; it is aimed at no earlier than December 2026 from pad 39A in Florida. Marked as gone quiet until SpaceX announces something.

threads.title: US flights halted nationwide

updates.text: The FAA halted every US departure after a communications failure hit the en-route control centres. About 1.5 million travellers stranded. Homeland Security: no sign of an attack.
Flights back after about 4 hours (3:54 to 8:15 pm Eastern); over 15,000 flights hit. Cause still disputed: overloaded routers or system updates, depending on which official is speaking.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the root cause is still unknown. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says it began while a contractor, L3Harris, moved old copper phone lines to fiber; L3Harris says it is helping the investigation. Officials say there is no sign of a cyberattack. Saturday cancellations passed 5,000.

The Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) first review points to two sites: a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where L3Harris was installing a new router, and a radar site in Amarillo, Texas. Blocking both calmed the network. The FAA has switched off a broadcasting feature on all the new routers. Officials still do not say whether it was human error or a faulty router. Flights were close to normal by Sunday.

Monday morning: 284 US flights cancelled and 954 delayed (FlightAware), mostly American Airlines. Since Friday the total is about 18,520 cancelled and over 28,300 delayed. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy repeated on Sunday there is no sign of a cyberattack.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says a router is the "likely cause"; a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) team is at contractor L3Harris's lab in Florida, and he asked the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to help. Juniper Networks, maker of the Arkansas router, says its device "did not fail". Duffy repeated his ask for $50 billion; Senators Jack Reed, Ted Cruz and leader John Thune questioned the number. Flighty counts over 17,000 cancellations Friday to Sunday, the worst technology-caused disruption on record. Monday: 347 cancelled by 6 pm.

The Wall Street Journal reports (as quoted by other outlets) that the Arkansas unit was a new Juniper router installed by L3Harris, and officials believe a feature that broadcast data too widely caused the overload. Duffy says a second router, in Amarillo, Texas, then flooded the network. Engineers from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Juniper and Cisco are testing the equipment in Florida. The FAA has not given a final cause and no cyberattack has been found.

Secretary of State Rubio says there is no evidence linking the recent Microsoft, Federal Aviation Administration and bank disruptions to cyberattacks. See the new story on the National Security Agency network outage.

threads.title: Iran presses on US bases

updates.text: The US moved tanker aircraft and Ospreys out of RAF Mildenhall in England over a reported Iranian threat. Bases raised to a higher protection level.
US forces shot down 2 Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain, home of the US Fifth Fleet. First Iranian shot at a Gulf base in two months. No damage.
Iran calls it payback for a US strike in southern Iran and claims it hit a US radar; the US denies it. No US strike back found.

Second attack on Bahrain in three days. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say six drones went for a US air defence radar at the Al-Riffa helicopter base. Bahrain sounded its first nationwide alert since September and says it shot the attack down. No damage or casualties reported; no US statement yet. Saudi Arabia also reported Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh, intercepted.

The US military gives a different count for Sunday's attack on Bahrain: it says the Revolutionary Guards launched two one-way attack drones, not six, and US forces shot both down. Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemned Iran.

Third claimed attack on Bahrain in five days. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say their drones hit a US-run radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base, saying US drones keep crossing into Iranian airspace. Bahrain sounded a shelter alert and explosions were heard over Manama. Bahrain's armed forces say they destroyed the attackers before they reached their target. No US statement found yet. Separately, a third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, is now in the region; US Central Command (CENTCOM) calls it a scheduled rotation. Qatar urged all sides to hold back.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) now says Tuesday's drones were intercepted, with no damage to US equipment and no Americans hurt; it did not say how many. Iran's claim of a hit on the radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base is contradicted. An International Crisis Group analyst says Iran is signalling it will answer even US flights near its airspace, not only attacks. Qatar, a mediator, was due to meet Iranian officials Tuesday; peace talks are stalled.

The fight spread to a fourth country. US officials told Fox News and others that US jets struck an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday, "in self-defense". A local Iranian official says there was no damage to infrastructure. On Wednesday, Iran's army said its drones hit Patriot air defence systems at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. Kuwait says it was intercepting the drones and reported no damage; US Central Command had not commented. Egypt, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait.

Israel's Channel 13 reports Prime Minister Netanyahu told a security meeting that an operation against Iran is "unavoidable", and that Israeli and US Central Command (CENTCOM) plans are ready, with timing up to Trump. Channel 13 also says Israel's military told both leaders there is no immediate need to strike. One outlet at the root; not confirmed by the Israeli government.

Trump told Fox News from Shenzhen there are indications Iran is looking at gases and biological weapons, but he did not think Washington should be alarmed, and said the US would wipe them out if it attacked. The New York Times reports Netanyahu urged a joint US and Israeli air campaign of four to seven days; Trump has not approved it. Axios says US and Israeli officials think Iran has expanded chemical weapons research but cannot carry out such attacks now. Iran's Foreign Ministry calls the claims fraudulent. A Pentagon official puts the cost of the war to the US military at more than $48 billion since late February.
A Times of Israel headline says Trump is not rushing into a strike and will wait until January. Only that one outlet found for the January timing.

Trump now says a decision on fresh strikes on Iran can wait until after the start of 2027 (this replaces the single-outlet January claim from the last scan). The Senate rejected a resolution to curb the military campaign, 48 to 51. US Central Command (CENTCOM) denied carrying out any new strike on Qeshm Island on Friday, after Iranian media reported an explosion or missile hit there; the cause is not established.

Iranian state TV showed the Revolutionary Guard unveiling a new launcher at an underground site that it says can fire two liquid-fuelled missiles, a message against US claims that the missile programme was destroyed. Iran's deputy foreign minister says mediators from Qatar visited on Friday to see "whether another opportunity can be given to diplomacy". Trump says Iran will not make an acceptable deal.

Bahrain says an Iranian attack set fire to a civilian industrial site; The National reports two people hurt, one critically. Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it fired missiles and drones at US positions at the Riffa and Awali bases. Trump said there is an "indication" Iran is looking at chemical or biological weapons; Iran's foreign ministry rejected that. CBS reports Trump says he wants a "permanent" deal and that his next move may not come until 2027.

The Associated Press (AP), via PBS, says Iran fired drones at a US radar site in Bahrain, its third attack on US military targets there in recent days after about two months of calm. Bahrain says shrapnel caused minor damage and no injuries in Sunday's attack on Riffa and Awali. Iran's army also claims a missile damaged a US F-16 jet over the Gulf and forced it to land; US Central Command (CENTCOM) says Iran did not attack any F-16 "at all" and all US jets are accounted for. Trump says he is "inclined" to restart full bombing of Iran after the New Year.
No new attack on US bases found since Sunday's drone attack in Bahrain. Iran says it will use all means against the blockade.
No new Iranian attack on US bases found since the 21 Nov strikes in Bahrain.
No new Iranian attack on US bases found since Sunday's drone attack in Bahrain. Reporting this week has shifted to the strait and to whether the US or Israel will strike Iran itself.
No new base attack confirmed today. Iran continues to deny a drone strike on a Kuwaiti military site that killed two Italian nationals.

threads.title: Strait of Hormuz: tankers hit, oil up

updates.text: Explosions hit 4 oil tankers in the strait. Brent crude near $94 a barrel.
Ship traffic is a trickle: about 3 ships a day against 85 before the war. Oil near $96. Iran says the tankers ignored warnings (not verified).
Brent crude closed Friday at $95.84 a barrel. Traders will react when futures reopen Sunday evening.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three oil tankers hit sea mines in the strait and caught fire. The ships were not named and nobody has verified it. The US says the main routes are cleared of mines.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards now say two more tankers hit mines on Monday 16 Nov, and that one supertanker carrying over two million barrels sank. Iran's count is six tankers in two days. None of it is verified and no ship has been named. US Central Command (CENTCOM) says the strait has been swept clear.

More ship damage reported by an independent monitor. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) reported on 16 Nov a tanker hit by an "unknown projectile" with an engine room fire, crew safe, and later a disabled tanker with an engine room fire north of Khasab, Oman. UKMTO named neither ship. Iran's Guards claim yet another mine hit on Tuesday morning, with no evidence. Iran's mine story and its count of six or more tankers are still unproven, and the US says the shipping lanes are clear. Iran and Oman's foreign ministers met in Muscat about keeping ships safe.

A named ship this time: the Panama-flagged gas tanker Tara Gas was hit on 16 Nov and again on 17 Nov, and its crew abandoned ship. Of 25 crew, 21 were taken ashore at Khasab, Oman, two are in hospital and one Indian sailor is missing. India's foreign ministry condemned the attack. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) counts at least 15 attacks on ships in or near the strait this month. Who fired on Tara Gas is not stated.

Iran's army says the strait stays closed to ships using what it calls unauthorised routes. Iran also claims another tanker hit a sea mine east of the strait and caught fire; no independent confirmation found. The US strike on Qeshm Island, which sits inside the strait, was aimed at missile launchers (US officials). No new attack confirmed by the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre since the Tara Gas.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) confirms a tanker was hit by a projectile in its engine room while leaving the strait on Wednesday evening; a security firm names it the Navig8 Messi. All crew safe. Separately, Iran's army claims three tankers hit sea mines in the eastern strait and caught fire; not independently confirmed. The US military says it has cleared the main routes of mines.

Splash247 says the tanker hit near Khasab, the Navig8 Messi run by Abu Dhabi's ADNOC Logistics and Services, has one seafarer missing and 11 injured. Bloomberg counts at least two seafarers missing after this week's attacks and says attacks have run at a higher pace since October. Iran's Revolutionary Guards, through the Tasnim agency, claim two supertankers exploded after hitting naval mines; no neutral source confirms it.

More ships hit. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) office says two outbound tankers were hit by unidentified projectiles near Khasab, Oman on Saturday 21 Nov, one about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, with no casualties reported. On Friday a tanker 8 nautical miles north of Khasab reported a fire; Iran's Revolutionary Guards say it hit a mine. Iran's foreign minister says the US blockade of Iranian ports must end before Iran can resume oil exports.

AP now counts at least three tankers attacked in or near the strait on Saturday. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre says two outbound tankers were hit by projectiles, one in the stern and one in the engine room, with no casualties reported. Iran's navy says a third tanker hit a naval mine east of the strait before noon and caught fire. Iranian state media say the navy ran its most "intense and varied" operations yet overnight to stop ships, aimed at the US escorts.

No new ship attacks found since Saturday's. Counts for Saturday still differ: the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre says two tankers were hit by projectiles; other outlets count three. Iran says every ship must follow lanes it sets; the US is blockading Iranian ports and escorting tankers.

Trump dared Iran to test the US blockade and said any ships that try will be sunk. Iranian media say 14 tankers are waiting at Kharg Island to run it; there is no confirmation they have been ordered to sail. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre reported a tanker "involved in an incident with military forces" in the Gulf of Oman near Chabahar, without saying what happened. Iran's foreign ministry says it will use "every means" against the blockade. Brent oil was about $91.70 on Monday morning, after a third weekly fall.

Iran's army chief ordered the navy to close the strait "further day by day" until the US meets Iran's demands. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers hit mines; the Joint Maritime Information Centre (JMIC) says that is not verified, keeps the threat level at severe, and says more attacks are highly likely. Reports of a 14-tanker convoy to run the blockade remain unconfirmed. Qatar is pushing to restart talks. Brent oil is near a three-month low, about $89.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy says two more tankers hit mines and caught fire on Wednesday after using an unauthorized route. That is Iran's claim; we found no independent confirmation. CNN, citing maritime data, says attacks on shipping are at the highest level since the war began. The US Treasury added sanctions on more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses and front companies. Oil traders shrugged it off: Brent settled at $91.40 on Tuesday and was near $90 early Wednesday. A claim on one aggregator site that oil passed $120 is not supported by any market report we found.

The head of Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said the Strait of Hormuz is now under Iran's "complete control". The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) and other monitors count about 25 ships hit in and around the strait over the past week, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes. Iran's demands include ending the war, unfreezing its assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of its ports. Brent oil held near a three-month low, about $90 a barrel.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two more oil tankers were hit by sea mines north of the Omani port of Khasab while crossing the Strait of Hormuz, the latest in near-daily claims. The United States said it struck Qeshm Island in self-defence after Iranian attacks on Bahrain. Ship transits stay well down and crude leaving the Gulf is about half of pre-war levels, Kpler says, with oil reported near 85 to 95 dollars a barrel.

threads.title: Ukraine war: Moscow airports shut by drones

updates.text: Strikes both ways: blackouts in Ukraine, drones over Moscow.
All four Moscow airports shut. Moscow's mayor says more than 100 drones were shot down (Russian figure, not verified).

Zelenskyy says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would leave Donbas in return for joining NATO (the North Atlantic Treaty Organization). The US has not confirmed it; the Kremlin has not answered. Zelenskyy says any land deal would go to a national vote. Russia sent 117 drones at Ukraine overnight, killing at least two.

More detail on the Abu Dhabi talks: they ended without a breakthrough, but both sides agreed a prisoner swap of more than 1,000 people. Zelenskyy says Ukraine proposed a local truce for seven or eight front line villages where civilians are trapped.

Russia's defence ministry says it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones over 16 regions, the most in one night of the war (Russian figure). Crimea's Russian-installed governor says the bridge to Crimea was hit; the Kremlin calls the damage minor and road traffic was halted for repairs. Refineries and industrial sites were also hit; six people injured in Ilsky. Zelenskyy says the refinery strikes cut over half of Russia's refining capacity (not verified). Ukraine has not commented on the bridge.

Ukraine's General Staff says its drones hit the Ilsky oil refinery in southern Russia. The Crimean Bridge was shut to vehicles, then partly reopened. One Ukrainian outlet (UA News) says Russia now claims 1,441 drones downed; not confirmed elsewhere, and all Russian counts are unverified. Russia hit a cardboard factory in Odesa with a jet drone.

Part of the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge has fallen into the sea. Checked videos show a section down; Ukraine's security service (SBU) says one metal arch and the road span under it were destroyed and the rail line damaged, after attacks on Monday and again overnight. Zelenskyy calls it a response to Russian strikes on Ukraine's power and infrastructure. Russia opened a "terrorist act" case and the Kremlin says it will rebuild. Road traffic is stopped; some trains resumed Tuesday. Crimea's Russian-installed head says two people were killed nearby. Overnight Russia damaged two main bridges in Kyiv, killing two, and hit the power grid in eight regions.

Zelenskyy says Ukrainian-made Palianytsia drones hit the road part of the Kerch Bridge and Neptune missiles hit the rail part, after weeks of preparation. Ukraine's General Staff says the road section is out of service. CNN says the damage looks worse than in earlier attacks. Russia calls it a terrorist act and claims it shot down 1,441 Ukrainian drones overnight (Russian figure, not checked). Russian state media TASS says rail traffic has resumed and some road traffic is moving one way at a time; not independently confirmed.

A third Ukrainian strike in four days halted rail traffic on the Kerch Bridge, says the Moscow-appointed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov; he expects trains to restart around 4 pm local time. The road deck was already out. Hours later, Ukraine's European allies, Zelenskyy and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner were due in Berlin for talks on security guarantees.

Putin, speaking in China, said Russia will not negotiate a limited ceasefire (he had weighed limits on naval attacks and on strikes on energy sites) because of the Kerch Bridge strikes, and promised a much more painful response. In Berlin, Kushner said Russia had accepted that any guarantee for Ukraine would rest on a model like NATO's Article 5 (an attack on one is an attack on all). Russia's deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov rejected that the next day. Zelenskyy said Berlin produced no shared view of what such guarantees would mean.

Hours after Putin promised revenge for the Kerch Bridge strikes, Russia fired a huge overnight missile and drone attack on Ukraine. In Kyiv the Podilskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges over the Dnipro were damaged and power, heating and water were cut. Counts of the dead differ as they rise: Al Jazeera says at least 8 across Ukraine, the Kyiv Independent at least 9. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted bridges used to move weapons. Some missiles and drones came down in Poland; see the new story on that.

A Russian ballistic missile strike on the centre of Kryvyi Rih, Zelenskyy's home town, killed a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman and wounded 60, including six children. The city head says three more rockets hit as rescuers arrived. Separately, a Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad caught fire in the Gulf of Finland after a drone hit, Finnish and Russian officials say; who struck it is not established. Zelenskyy called the Kerch Bridge strikes a "fair response" to Russian attacks on Ukrainian bridges.

Lviv's mayor says a Russian missile and drone attack on Friday morning killed two people; reports give 7 to 10 injured. It hit homes, an energy site and the ticket hall of Sknyliv railway station. Al Jazeera showed dashcam video of a missile hitting a street. Al Jazeera also reports at least four killed in strikes on Odesa.

The Moscow Times reports a Ukrainian drone strike on an oil refinery in Russia's Perm region that killed one person, and Russian drone attacks on the Kyiv region that killed at least four. NBC lists a third Ukrainian strike in a week on the Crimean bridge and a prisoner exchange. Biggest news of the day is a separate story: Ukraine says it sank a Russian warship in Libya.

Al Jazeera reports Russia fired more than 400 drones and 110 missiles across Ukraine overnight, killing at least 14 people in the Kyiv region. Odesa was reported without power, heat and water after strikes. Ukraine is asking the US to release more Patriot air defence missiles.

President Zelensky confirmed Ukraine hit the Russian cargo ship Sparta II with drones in the Gulf of Finland on 21 Nov, calling it a legitimate target carrying weapons. Norway, a firm Ukraine ally, urged caution near its region. Overnight into Wednesday, Ukraine's Air Force says Russia sent 112 drones and 88 were downed. In Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said drone debris started a fire that killed two people.

Zelensky said that if Trump's push for a deal by year's end fails, he will go to the incoming US Congress in January to seek more military aid and tougher sanctions on Russia. Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are trying to broker a deal "as soon as possible", with January seen as the target. Trump laughed off the January timing and said he has set no deadline, adding that sometimes Putin looks ready and Zelensky is not. The Trump team has reportedly shelved offering Russia business deals as an incentive, after Moscow stayed focused on taking territory.
No fresh Moscow airport closure reported today, though Russian strikes on Ukraine and long-range drone exchanges continue.

threads.title: Bitcoin slides as bond rates jump

updates.text: Bitcoin under $70,000 and US stocks slid after a hot inflation report. $1.3 billion in crypto bets wiped out.
Bitcoin near $68,000, lowest since August. US 10-year bond rate hit 5.13%.
Bitcoin kept falling on Saturday, touching about $63,300, its lowest since mid-August. The 10-year bond rate ended Friday near 5.13%.
Bitcoin dipped to about $62,000 over the weekend, then climbed back to about $65,000 on Monday. Crypto trade sites point to money leaving Bitcoin funds and fear of higher interest rates.
Bitcoin slipped back to about $64,000 (Fortune: $64,013 at 7:30 am Eastern on Monday). It was near $64,200 early Tuesday as US stock futures pointed lower before Nvidia's results.
Bitcoin did not join the stock bounce: about $64,100, down 1.1% since midnight UTC (Coordinated Universal Time), CoinDesk says. That is about 26% below its October high.
Bitcoin fell after the Federal Reserve minutes, to roughly $62,300 to $62,500 (sources differ), down about 3 to 4% on the day.
Bitcoin fell below $62,000, touching about $61,500 to $61,700 (reports differ), as stocks slid.

Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July and kept falling overnight, to about $55,600 early Saturday, its lowest since September 2024. Business Recorder had it at $55,830 at 04:13 UTC. Crypto news sites point to money pulled out of bitcoin funds and forced selling of borrowed bets.

Bitcoin fell as low as about $55,150 early Saturday, then bounced to about $57,900 by 10:00 UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). More than $2.5 billion of borrowed bets were forced closed in 24 hours. Figures differ by exchange and time.

After touching about $55,130 on Saturday, its lowest since September 2024, bitcoin bounced to roughly $59,000 by Sunday morning (quotes range $58,900 to $60,400 by exchange). It is still down about 12% on the week.
Bitcoin climbed back above $61,000 on Monday as stock futures bounced, with a high near $61,850. It had touched about $55,000 on Saturday.
Bitcoin did not join the stock rally. It ended the US trading day about flat near $61,250, briefly topped $64,000, then slipped back below $60,000 in Asian trading.
Bitcoin fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday, about $59,700 to $59,900 depending on the source, giving back most of the run toward $64,000.

Bitcoin slid further, trading in the high $58,000s to about $60,000 on Tuesday depending on the source, and down on the week. One market fear gauge read "extreme fear". Ethereum, XRP and Solana also fell.

Bitcoin is trading in the high 50,000s to low 60,000s of dollars, swinging with the technology stocks. It briefly topped 61,000 dollars on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, then slipped back below 60,000. Exchange-traded fund outflows hit a record 4.71 billion dollars for November, a sign of steady selling.

threads.title: Nvidia boss Jensen Huang resigns, then returns

updates.text: Resigned effective immediately (company filing). Finance chief Colette Kress is interim chief executive. Shares fell as much as 13%, then bounced.
Nothing new found.
Nothing new dated this weekend.

The Financial Times reports Jensen Huang is talking with allies about coming back as chief executive; one ally describes a 'war room' of tech bosses. Neither Huang nor Nvidia has confirmed. Shares slipped about 2% before the market opened on Monday.

Reports say the board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back. The Commerce Department issued a rule requiring a licence to send advanced chips to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, to stop Chinese firms renting that computing power through data centres there. Nvidia fell about 4% to its lowest close since July 2025. Its quarterly results are due Tuesday 17 Nov.

Nvidia shares fell about 4% on Monday to their lowest close since July 2025 (CNBC). Reports still say the board is not considering bringing Huang back; an online petition for his return passed 190,000 signatures. Results come out after the market closes today, the first without Huang. Interim chief executive Colette Kress, the finance chief, leads. Analysts expect revenue near $109 billion.

updates.when: 17 Nov, after the close (about 4:20 pm Eastern)
updates.text: First results without Jensen Huang: revenue $115.8 billion for the quarter to 25 Oct, up 103% on a year ago and above the roughly $109 billion analysts expected. Data centre revenue a record $107.6 billion. Nvidia expects about $130 billion next quarter and assumes no data centre chip sales to China. Interim chief executive Colette Kress: "Our momentum is real." Board chair Harvey Jones says the board "does not intend to reinstate" Huang; a search firm is looking for a permanent chief. A new board committee will oversee export rules. Shares closed at $155.46, then rose up to about 4% after hours (5% by the end of the call, NBC).

The Wall Street Journal reports the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has opened a civil probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors; neither the SEC nor Nvidia has confirmed it. Nvidia's chairman says the company is not thinking of bringing Huang back. After the strong results, Nvidia shares were up about 3% before Wednesday's open; the company also added $150 billion to its share buyback.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

California's attorney general served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena, looking at whether China got Nvidia's advanced chips or secret information and whether investors were misled (reported by Bloomberg via Benzinga). CNBC says Treasury Secretary Bessent gave the board 10 days to answer questions, and that shareholders have begun suing.

Reuters reports, from two people briefed, that enforcement staff at the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) are looking at possible accounting issues at Nvidia; the SEC declined to comment and an inquiry is not proof of wrongdoing. Nvidia stock fell 13.8% on Friday to $125.53, its worst day since January 2025. Huang wrote on X that he would be honored to return if the board wants him; Trump said he would like Huang to apologize and go back. The Wall Street Journal says the board is not considering it.

No new official statement from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) or Nvidia. Weekend aggregator reports say Treasury Secretary Bessent accused Nvidia of knowingly selling chips to China; we could not find that remark at a major outlet, so treat it as UNPROVEN.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS "Face the Nation" the government still needs answers from Nvidia on chip sales to China. He said officials have spoken to the interim leaders, the board and lawyers, and want to know who ran compliance and whether knowledge went "all the way to the top". He asked whether Megaspeed, a Singapore company, was a front. One report says Nvidia was given 10 days; we found that only in one outlet. Nvidia futures rose about 6% before Monday's open.

Nvidia's board brought Jensen Huang back as president, chief executive officer (CEO) and board director, effective at once, in a unanimous vote. Chair Harvey Jones said the board was satisfied with his candor. The board says it took input from senior US government officials and found his return poses no national security risk; several outlets report the reversal came at President Trump's urging. Colette Kress goes back to being chief financial officer. The board's own investigation into a foreign intelligence effort aimed at Huang continues. The stock closed up 31.5% at $165.05, its best day since 2003, adding nearly $1 trillion in value.

Nvidia stock gave back some of Monday's jump, closing down about 5.9% at $155.38 on Tuesday. The board says its investigation of the foreign intelligence effort aimed at Huang will run to the end. updates.text: A Learjet 60 business jet (registration N722BD, built 2004) dived from about 35,000 feet and hit Military Trail at 10th Avenue North in unincorporated Palm Beach County, near Greenacres, a few miles south of the main West Palm Beach airport. All nine people on board died: two crew and seven passengers. It was a charter flight from Austin, Texas, to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas, run by Aurora Aviation of Fort Lauderdale, which trades as Upper Jets. It missed homes in the Greenacres Mobile Home Community by feet and left a crater in the road. One person in a passing car was hurt. A dashcam filmed the impact.

A family spokesperson named the passengers: Austin technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp, their young children Emma and Charlie Robinson, family friends Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, and the children's nanny Anita Maria Cetina. The captain was Jeff Gregory; the first officer was Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, 20, of Boca Raton. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) records show she held a commercial pilot certificate and a rating to fly the Learjet 60 as second in command, not as captain. It is the deadliest Learjet 60 crash on record.

updates.when: 2 and 3 Nov, National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) briefings

Air traffic audio shows the crew reported light clear ice and moderate turbulence at about 35,000 feet, with height swings of about 700 feet, and asked to climb to 37,000 feet. Then came an overspeed, a mayday call and a dive faster than 20,000 feet a minute. The FAA says the jet fell from 35,250 to 8,750 feet in one minute. Thunderstorms were in the area. The NTSB says weather is a main focus but has not said it caused the crash.

updates.when: 4 to 9 Nov, digging out the crater

The NTSB asked anyone holding debris, including pieces found on roofs, not to keep or move it and to email witness@ntsb.gov. By 8 Nov it had recovered parts of both wings, both engines, the flight deck, the vertical and horizontal tail, the left elevator, aileron sections and flap tracks; some went to its Washington laboratories. On 9 Nov it said the cockpit voice recorder had been found at the impact point and the dig was finished. The recorder is being checked in the NTSB lab; whether it captured usable audio has not been said.

About 600 residents of the mobile home community were evacuated or displaced; shelters opened and United Way set up a relief fund. John I. Leonard High School, next to the site, closed on 2 Nov and reopened later that week. Residents began going home around 9 Nov. Military Trail, cut by the crater, reopened in both directions on 12 Nov after repairs, the Florida Department of Transportation said.

No new NTSB statement since 9 Nov. No cause has been named. The NTSB usually issues a preliminary report about 30 days after a crash, which would be around early December, but it has not announced a date. A final report with the probable cause usually takes one to two years. No lawsuit or FAA action on the Learjet 60 was found in this scan.

threads.title: Anthropic mathematician claims a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

updates.text: Levent Alpoge, a mathematician on Anthropic's staff, posted a four-page note on his website saying he and the AI model Claude found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, the 1859 problem about how prime numbers are spread out and one of seven $1 million Millennium Prize Problems. The proof is in 17 million lines of Lean, a language a computer can check line by line. Nobody outside has checked it yet: the Clay Mathematics Institute still lists it as unsolved and says checking takes time, while calling the announcement of "historic significance". Anthropic did not answer AP. In August, a Claude result on the same zeta function was a partial step, not a proof.

Big step. The Lean and Mathlib communities, the people behind the main computer proof checker, issued a joint statement that they have "full confidence" the proof is correct. The proof is about 17 million lines of Lean code; it checks against Mathlib's own standard statement of the hypothesis, and MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) mathematician Andrew Sutherland rebuilt it himself with no errors. Science reports many mathematicians expect it to hold up, but people still need weeks to understand the ideas. A separate, human-written proof claim also surfaced; nobody has checked that one yet.

The journal Nature says mathematicians are astounded but split. There is still no human-readable paper, only the computer proof and a 4-page sketch. Number theorist Andrew Granville says a clear write-up should have come first. One critic argues a condition in the code is always true, which would make the result empty; Lean experts are checking that on their forum and it is not settled. James Maynard expects the proof to hold. Anthropic itself has not posted about it.

Reporting ties it to a wider wave: a breach of an unclassified open-source system used by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), which CNN's sources say does not appear linked, and a separate "cybersecurity incident" at the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).

No new development. The Federal Bureau of Investigation is still investigating a suspected breach of the National Crime Information Center, reported on 21 November. Sources say it does not appear linked to the Central Intelligence Agency and Treasury breaches.

threads.title: Manchester: arena evacuated after unknown substance released

updates.when: 22 Nov, about 10 pm UK time (5 pm Eastern)
updates.text: About 12,000 people were evacuated from the Co-op Live arena during a Don Toliver concert after an "unknown substance" was let off in the crowd. Police first said it was believed to be tear gas, then called it unknown. More than 50 people were treated for eye and breathing problems and one went to hospital. Police are investigating.
Greater Manchester Police say tests are still under way to find out what the substance was and where it came from. The arena is still a police scene.

Greater Manchester Police say the investigation into the unknown substance continues, with the substance still not identified. Police say 89 people showed symptoms and one woman was taken to hospital. They are looking at whether the release was linked to a string of jewellery robberies during the Don Toliver concert, with nine separate theft reports. No arrests so far.

Tests on the unknown substance released at the Don Toliver concert are still ongoing. Police are now examining whether the release was a deliberate diversion for a string of jewellery robberies, with nine thefts reported during the show. About 80 to 89 people were treated for eye irritation and one was taken to hospital. No arrests have been made and the arena is being decontaminated.

threads.title: Storms on both US coasts for Thanksgiving

updates.text: Forecasters expect a storm to form in the Southeast on Wednesday and grow into a major Northeast storm on Thanksgiving Day, with rain, wind and some wet snow in the Appalachians. Pacific storms bring heavy rain and Cascades snow late Wednesday into Thursday. Tuesday looks like the best travel day. Boston has very high tides on Thursday and Friday.

The storm is forming off Florida and peaks in the Northeast on Thanksgiving Day. Forecasters expect gusts over 50 mph, up to 60 mph on the coast, and the National Weather Service (NWS) warns of record high tides and major coastal flooding. Newark, LaGuardia and Washington National airports could see big delays. AAA (the American Automobile Association) expects about 81 million people to travel.

The storm arrived. Roughly 60 to 70 million people from the Southeast up to New England faced coastal flooding, high winds and heavy rain on Thanksgiving Day. The National Weather Service (NWS) forecast moderate to major coastal flooding and record-high tides, with wind gusts up to about 65 miles per hour at the shore. All major airlines issued travel waivers for the Northeast. The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York was postponed to Saturday, a rare move, because of the wind threat.

The storm hit hard. More than 700,000 people lost power, flights were delayed and cancelled, and the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was pushed to Saturday. Charleston reached major flood stage and New York's Central Park recorded its wettest Thanksgiving on record. Winter storm warnings covered parts of Missouri and Illinois with up to 13 inches of snow. Friday brings leftover wind and rain to the Northeast, then a separate Pacific storm aims at the West Coast this weekend.

threads.title: Magnitude 6.4 earthquake, Mauritius and Reunion region
threads.place: Indian Ocean, Mauritius and Reunion region

updates.text: The United States Geological Survey (USGS) recorded a magnitude 6.4 earthquake about 10 km deep in the Indian Ocean, in the Mauritius and Reunion region, with a green alert (little damage expected). The European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) puts it at 5.9. The spot is on the ocean ridge, far from the islands. No damage reports found.
No damage reports.
No damage reports.
No new development or damage reports from the magnitude 6.4 earthquake in the Mauritius and Reunion region.

threads.title: Hackers hit a CIA intelligence system; Treasury crime unit goes offline

updates.text: Hackers got into an unclassified system the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) use to gather and study public information, the New York Times and CNN report. Officials say no classified systems were touched. CNN's sources say early signs point to China; that is not confirmed. The same day the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) said it found unauthorized access to some systems and took them offline as a precaution, extending filing deadlines. Nobody has claimed either attack. Reports that the CIA problem was a faulty software update mix it up with the earlier National Security Agency (NSA) outage.

The Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) said it is investigating a "cybersecurity incident" that affected some of its services. The breach of the unclassified open-source system used by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) is still under investigation; officials say no classified networks were touched and the attackers have not been named.

More detail on the twin breaches. An unclassified system used by the Central Intelligence Agency was hacked, with no disruption to classified systems, and early signs point to China, two sources told reporters, though attribution is unconfirmed. The Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network took some systems offline after unauthorised access. Sources said an artificial-intelligence hacking tool called Artex may have been used.

threads.title: Pakistan's first astronaut reaches China's space station
threads.place: Tiangong space station (launched from Jiuquan, China)

updates.text: China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft docked with the Tiangong space station carrying Muhammad Zeeshan Ali of Pakistan, the first astronaut from another country to visit it. He is expected to stay about a week, then fly home with two of the Shenzhou-23 crew, while Zhu Yangzhu stays on for a year-long mission.
No new development. Pakistan's first astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, is aboard China's Tiangong space station for about a week.

The mission is going to plan. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Pakistan's first astronaut and the first from any country to visit China's Tiangong station, is aboard for about a week before flying home with two of the earlier crew.

threads.title: Cartagena: gunmen take supermarket hostages, troops free them

updates.text: After a failed robbery of an armored truck, gunmen ran into an Exito supermarket in Cartagena and took about 25 to 30 hostages. Ten were let go during the standoff. Security forces stormed the store early Wednesday and President Abelardo de la Espriella says all hostages were rescued. We found no confirmed figure for any injuries.
No new figures. Colombian security forces rescued the hostages from the Exito supermarket and the president said all were freed.
No new development. Colombian forces freed all hostages from the Cartagena supermarket siege; one captor was killed.

threads.title: Small plane crashes off Mississippi, six killed

updates.text: A Cessna 210 flying from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida, went down in the Gulf about 2 miles from Horn Island. The Coast Guard says all six aboard died, four adults and two boys aged 8 and 10. Early Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) data shows a very fast descent before contact was lost. The NTSB is investigating; no cause has been given.
No change. All six aboard the Cessna 210, four adults and two boys, were confirmed dead; the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating.
No new development. All six aboard the Cessna 210 that crashed off Mississippi were confirmed dead; the National Transportation Safety Board is investigating.

threads.title: US clears SpaceX for up to one million satellites in space

updates.text: The Federal Communications Commission authorised SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites to build data centres in orbit. The order says SpaceX must launch at least one authorised space station by 2033, then add more gradually through 2040. Scientists are divided: astrophysicist and author Adam Becker called the idea 'a fantasy', and astronomers worry about crowding and light pollution in orbit.

threads.title: Ukraine downs a Russian jet drone with a laser, a world first

updates.text: A Ukrainian adviser said the home-made Blysk laser shot down a fast jet-powered Geran attack drone, which Ukraine says is the first time in the world a combat laser has done so. A video said to show the intercept was posted online but has not been independently verified. Ukraine had been struggling to stop these faster drones, so a cheap laser defence would matter if it can be scaled up.

threads.title: Germany arrests two over an Iran-linked synagogue plot

updates.text: German police arrested two Iraqi men accused of belonging to a group that United States and British officials link to Iran's Revolutionary Guard. Prosecutors say operatives carrying explosives approached two synagogues on consecutive nights in late March but did not strike. Seventeen locations were searched. The men have not been tried, and the claims are prosecutors' allegations.
